_meta.description: Co-celebrated saints Liturgy overlay: secondary troparion/kontakion + 2nd prokeimenon/alleluia/gospel/communion hymn for dates where a major fixed-calendar commemoration falls on a Great Feast — also used for OCA-specific principal-feast Sundays (e.g. Synaxis of N.A. Saints on 6-14) that need a secondary saints' prokeimenon on top of the Sunday one.
_meta._note: Keys are "M-D" date strings. Second epistle/gospel are pulled from orthocal readings[] automatically.
_meta.source: OCA Department of Liturgical Music and Translations service texts (Thee/Thy register).

1-1._note: Circumcision of our Lord falls on St. Basil the Great's feast day. OCA practice: Liturgy of St. Basil; troparion + kontakion of Basil sung alongside the Circumcision feast hymns (Glory: Basil's kontakion, Now: Circumcision's). Without this overlay only the Circumcision troparion/kontakion render and Basil's drop out of the Little Entrance section. Prokeimenon/alleluia/koinonikon added 2026-07-02 after judge sweep flagged them missing — Basil's secondary attaches on top of the Circumcision primary (which lives in great-feast-variants.json).

troparion.rubric: Troparion of St. Basil the Great, Tone 1:
troparion.text:
Thy proclamation has gone out into all the earth
which was divinely taught by hearing thy voice
expounding the nature of creatures,
ennobling the manners of men.
O holy father of a royal priesthood,
entreat Christ God to save our souls.

kontakion.rubric: Kontakion of St. Basil the Great, Tone 4:
kontakion.connector: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.
kontakion.text:
Thou wast revealed as the sure foundation of the Church,
granting all mankind a lordship which cannot be taken away,
sealing it with thy precepts,
O venerable and heavenly Father Basil.

prokeimenon.label: St. Basil the Great
prokeimenon.refrain: My mouth shall speak wisdom, and the meditation of my heart shall be of understanding.

alleluia.label: St. Basil the Great
verses: The mouth of the righteous shall meditate wisdom, and his tongue shall speak of judgment.

communionHymn.label: St. Basil the Great
communionHymn.text: The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance; he shall not be afraid of evil tidings. Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia!

troparion.rubric: Troparion of Sts. Constantine and Helen, Tone 8:
troparion.text:
Thy servant Constantine, O Lord and only Lover of man,
beheld the figure of the Cross in the heavens.
Like Paul, not having received his call from men,
but as an apostle among rulers set by Thy hand over the royal city,
he preserved lasting peace through the prayers of the Theotokos.

kontakion.rubric: Kontakion of Sts. Constantine and Helen, Tone 3:
kontakion.connector: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.
kontakion.text:
Today Constantine and his mother Helen reveal the precious Cross,
the weapon of Orthodox Christians against their enemies,
for it is manifest for us as a great and fearful sign in struggle.

prokeimenon.label: Sts. Constantine and Helen
prokeimenon.refrain: Their proclamation has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the universe.

alleluia.label: Sts. Constantine and Helen
verses: I have exalted one chosen out of My people.

communionHymn.label: Sts. Constantine and Helen
communionHymn.text: Their proclamation has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the universe. Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia!

6-14._note: Synaxis of All Saints of North America (2nd Sunday after Pentecost in the OCA). Adds the saints' prokeimenon and the saints' communion verse alongside the regular Sunday Tone 1 propers. Troparion/kontakion already come from the menaion DB (id 1196); not duplicated here.

prokeimenon.label: Synaxis of All Saints of North America
prokeimenon.refrain: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His saints.

communionHymn.label: Synaxis of All Saints of North America
communionHymn.text: Rejoice in the Lord, O you righteous; praise befits the just! Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia!

8-16._note: Translation of the Image Not-Made-by-Hands from Edessa to Constantinople, the third "Feast of the Savior in August" (8-16), which falls inside the Afterfeast of the Dormition. The OCA order for 2026-08-16 gives it its own troparion, kontakion, prokeimenon, alleluia and communion hymn alongside the Sunday and Dormition propers; before this entry none of them rendered. Troparion and kontakion are the menaion's own (variable-sources/menaion/august-16.json). The kontakion lands at "Glory..." immediately before the Dormition window's, which holds "Now and ever..." -- see the feastCycle branch in liturgy-from-orthocal.js. GAPS: the OCA order names the Image's prokeimenon (Tone 4, "Sing to the Lord a new song...") and alleluia (Tone 4) by incipit only, and no authoritative verse text is on hand, so neither is authored here rather than invented. The Sunday Tone-2 prokeimenon and alleluia render alone until those arrive.

troparion.rubric: Troparion of the Image Not-Made-by-Hands, Tone 2:
troparion.text: We bow down before Thy most pure image, O Good One, asking forgiveness of our transgressions, O Christ God; for of Thine own will Thou wast well pleased to ascend the Cross in the flesh, that Thou mightest deliver from slavery to the enemy those whom Thou hadst fashioned. Wherefore, we cry to Thee in thanksgiving: Thou hast filled all things with joy, O our Savior, when Thou camest to save the world.

kontakion.rubric: Kontakion of the Image Not-Made-by-Hands, Tone 2:
kontakion.connector: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.
kontakion.text: O uncircumscribable Word of the Father, knowing the victorious image, un-inscribed and divinely wrought, of Thine ineffable and divine dispensation towards mankind, of Thy true incarnation, we honor it with veneration.

communionHymn.label: Translation of the Image Not-Made-by-Hands
communionHymn.text: O Lord, we shall walk in the light of Thy countenance, and shall exult in Thy name forever. Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia!
